title.value: Draft supplier and customer invoices in accounting software via browser

introduction.value: A Claude Code agent drives Chrome to save emailed supplier invoices as drafts for an auto repair shop, later drafting customer invoices from work orders, with the owner reviewing each morning.

method.value: A Claude Code agent on a Mac mini drives an ordinary Chrome browser. It opens supplier invoice emails, reads the PDFs, finds or creates the vendor in the accounting software, enters amount and due date, and saves a draft. It records what it learns in skill files. Six weeks in, it also drafted customer invoices from work orders. The owner reviews each morning.

outcome.value: Over 90 days the error rate fell from about one in eight invoices to under one in 20, and the morning review dropped from 20 to 10 minutes. The source estimates 9–10 hours a month saved.

notes.value: The source puts running cost at about $45 a month for a dedicated device plus inference, but the figures look illustrative rather than measured, and drafts always need human approval.

source_text.body:
Draft supplier and customer invoices in accounting software via browser
A Claude Code agent drives Chrome to save emailed supplier invoices as drafts for an auto repair shop, later drafting customer invoices from work orders, with the owner reviewing each morning.
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
A Claude Code agent on a Mac mini drives an ordinary Chrome browser. It opens supplier invoice emails, reads the PDFs, finds or creates the vendor in the accounting software, enters amount and due date, and saves a draft. It records what it learns in skill files. Six weeks in, it also drafted customer invoices from work orders. The owner reviews each morning.
How it went
Over 90 days the error rate fell from about one in eight invoices to under one in 20, and the morning review dropped from 20 to 10 minutes. The source estimates 9–10 hours a month saved.
Worth knowing
The source puts running cost at about $45 a month for a dedicated device plus inference, but the figures look illustrative rather than measured, and drafts always need human approval.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Using Chrome, open the supplier invoices in my inbox from [date range] and save each one as a draft bill in [Xero, QuickBooks or other accounting software]. Don't approve or pay anything. When you're done, give me a list of the drafts with supplier, amount and due date, and flag any you were unsure about. Pause and show me before submitting or deleting anything.
Original source: https://www.aidoers.io/blog/a-claude-code-agent-automated-a-real-accounting-workflow-with-no-api
